chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Rifah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him, 'Do the people go out to Mina in the early morning?' He said, 'Yes, until sunset.' Because this report is to be understood in light of what we mentioned regarding those with excuses, such as the sick and others, and that which indicates this is what he narrated:

key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْأَعْذَارِ: One with a valid excuse (e.g., illness, weakness)
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina, a holy site near Mecca where pilgrims spend days of Hajj

ai.seo_question: When is it permissible to leave Mina after standing at Arafat?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the timing of the Farewell Tawaf and departure from Mina, establishing that leaving in the early morning is permissible until sunset. The text explicitly contextualizes this ruling for those with valid excuses (A'dhar), such as illness, distinguishing their flexibility from the general practice of delaying departure to perform the Farewell Tawaf. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential approach of balancing ritual obligations with practical ease for pilgrims facing impediments.
